alcazaba: The 11th-century Moorish fortress-palace, the best preserved in Spain: battlemented walls, arched gateways, courtyards with fountains and gardens of orange trees and jasmine, with views of the port and the Cathedral. You climb on foot up ramps and steps, steep in places.
gibralfaro: The 14th-century castle on top of the hill overlooking the city, with a walk along the walls from which you see everything: the Alcazaba, the Cathedral, the port, the bullring and the sea. Getting there is a 15–20-minute climb on foot from the Alcazaba, or take the bus.
teatro: The theatre built in the 1st century AD under Augustus, at the foot of the Alcazaba, only rediscovered in 1951. You see the semicircular tiers and the remains of the stage; next to it is the visitor centre with the finds.
catedral: The Renaissance cathedral nicknamed "La Manquita", "the one-armed lady", because one of its two towers was never finished. Inside are a carved wooden choir and many chapels. A separate guided tour takes you up onto the roof (about 200 steps).
picasso: The museum in the Buenavista Palace, in the city where Picasso was born in 1881: over 200 works donated by his family, from early drawings to ceramics, in a Renaissance palace with Roman and Phoenician remains in the basement.
pompidou: The Spanish branch of the Paris museum at the port, recognisable by its coloured glass "cube". The permanent collection has works by Picasso, Magritte, Frida Kahlo and Kandinsky, often alongside temporary exhibitions.
thyssen: A 16th-century palace in the heart of the centre, with the great collection of 19th-century Andalusian painting: landscapes, folk scenes, bullfights and portraits. Beneath the museum you see the archaeological remains of a Roman house.
atarazanas: The city's covered market, in a building that keeps a 14th-century Moorish gateway, with a stained-glass window depicting the history of Málaga. Stalls of fresh fish, fruit, olives, hams and cheese; inside are bars where you eat standing up.
larios: Calle Larios and Plaza de la Constitución

The city's most elegant pedestrian street, with pale late-19th-century façades, shops and cafés, running from Plaza de la Constitución down to the Paseo del Parque. Very busy in the evening and, at Christmas, famous for its lights.
muelle: The harbour quay turned into a promenade with shops, bars and restaurants, near the Pompidou. From here you see the ships, La Farola lighthouse and, above, the Alcazaba. To get there, cross the port road from the Paseo del Parque.
